instruction.text: Complete the sentence with the correct relative pronoun.

hint.text:
To decide which relative pronoun to use, you need to think about what the relative clause is referring to. Here are some examples:


It reminded me of Sophie, who has brown hair.

Harry has a dog, whose name is Digger.

I bought the jumper that has a star on it.

Kevin bought a bike, which he will paint green.

We went to France last year, when it was the school holidays.

David has a shed in the garden, where he makes sculptures.
hint.sound: To decide which relative pronoun to use, you need to think about what the relative clause is referring to. Here are some examples.

atoms.a: Is she the girl, blank, speaks French?
atoms.b: Is she the girl ((++who whose)) speaks French?

atoms.a: I have an older sister, blank, is always there for me.
atoms.b: I have an older sister, ((++who what)) is always there for me.

atoms.a: We have a neighbour, blank, dog is very old.
atoms.b: We have a neighbour, ((++whose which)) dog is very old.

atoms.a: The book is about a magician, blank, powers are special.
atoms.b: The book is about a magician, ((++whose which)) powers are special.

atoms.a: My dad is wearing the orange jumper blank, I gave him for his birthday.
atoms.b: My dad is wearing the orange jumper ((++that who)) I gave him for his birthday.

atoms.a: I miss our holiday from last year, blank, it was really sunny.
atoms.b: I miss our holiday from last year, ((++when who)) it was really sunny.

atoms.a: My grandparents house has an allotment, blank, they grow vegetables.
atoms.b: My grandparents house has an allotment, ((++where whose)) they grow vegetables.

atoms.a: The maths homework was on algebra, blank, was really difficult.
atoms.b: The maths homework was on algebra, ((++which whose)) was really difficult.
